Subject: Cross-platform auth, stream keys, and speakers' release for Dec webinar

Team / partners —

Locking in a few things for the Dec 21 webinar (BrightWave sponsorship): can you confirm the items below and call out anything I missed? I want to get everyone aligned before we open rehearsals next week.

Checklist & asks:
- Auth model: Zoom account-level recording + ON24 ingest. Which tokens do we need from each vendor (OAuth client vs JWT)? @emma, please confirm required token types and rotation TTL.
- Stream keys / RTMP: ON24 needs primary+failover endpoints for the encoder. ON24 / Brooklyn Studio, please provide endpoints and expected ingest format (H.264 baseline / AAC).
- Speaker releases: attached is a draft release for speakers and BrightWave. Who signs (speaker vs sponsor), and can we get DocuSign by end of day 12/13?
- Registration mapping: Lauren, map our registration form to ON24 fields (email, company, role, marketing opt-in). Any custom field limits?
- Rehearsal/test window: I'd like a 30 min RTMP test + 20 min dry run with speakers on 12/14 — propose 10:30–11:30 PT.

Attachments: draft_speaker_release.docx (draft for signatures).

Goal: signed releases + token exchange + RTMP test scheduled by 12/14 so we can run final rehearsal 12/20.

Thanks —
Mateo Alvarez
Field Marketing, Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0192
From: Emma Li <emma@zoombusiness.com>

Date: 2026-12-11T09:43:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Cross-platform auth, stream keys, and speakers' release for Dec webinar

Hi Mateo —

Thanks for the checklist. Quick notes from the Zoom side: 
- Preferred auth: OAuth 2.0 (account-level) for long-lived integrations; JWT is supported for server-to-server but we recommend OAuth and rotating access tokens every 30 days for security. If you need a temporary token for a single rehearsal, we can issue a scoped token valid for 72 hours.
- Recording settings: For webinar recordings we recommend "Host records to cloud" (enable auto-delete policy as required). If you want ON24 to ingest a live stream from Zoom, enable live streaming to custom RTMP and give us the endpoint.
- Meeting limits: Make sure the meeting/webinar cloud recording option is enabled on your account and that the host (redwood account owner) is set as the live-streaming host.

I can create an OAuth client for Redwood and share client_id + redirect for your engineering team. Let me know whether you want the 30-day rotating tokens or a one-off 72-hour token for rehearsals.

— Emma Li
Partner Engineer, Zoom
emma@zoombusiness.com

I'll also request an encoder profile from Brooklyn Studio; if they don't provide, we will share our recommended profile (H.264 5mbps, 30fps, AAC 128kbps).

— Ben

Thanks everyone — quick status update and a couple final asks: 

Status:
- Speaker releases: signed copies uploaded to Drive (see link below). BrightWave signed on sponsor block; three speakers signed individually. Attachment: speaker_release_signed.pdf.
- Zoom auth: Emma issued a temporary 72-hour token for our rehearsal window; infra validated RTMP-to-ON24 flow.
- ON24 RTMP test: successful on 12/14, ON24 sent test report. Attached: on24_rtmp_test_report.pdf. No packetization issues; one transient audio drift at 00:10 that we corrected by adjusting encoder buffer.
- Registration mapping: Lauren confirmed fields and added "sponsor_interest" as a custom boolean (we flagged for privacy retention).

Final asks before the live event (12/21):
1) Legal: Ben, please confirm there are no sponsor redlines outstanding (I believe none).
2) Ops: Brooklyn Studio — please confirm you will use the attached encoder profile for both primary and failover connections.
3) Produk: can we enable cloud recording retention for 180 days (BrightWave requested 90, but Legal prefers 180).

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_webinar_assets

I'll keep the rehearsal / dry-run schedule in the calendar and send invites for 12/20 final run. Great teamwork — close to green.

— Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Field Marketing, Redwood Inference
